casting_test._listen: Two candidates per character, same line. Pick one, write it into `cast` below, then generate the full cut.

ORIANE.direction: Movement I is fear, not fatigue — she is young and arguing and losing. Her closing voice-over is the opposite: spoken after the battle that kills her, tired to the bone and still unbroken. Slow it and drop the level; never soften the spine.

voice.note: Caedom must sound older than Oriane and calmer than everything around him; Alder must read a shade colder than Wren, because the last line of the film is his.

world_language.note: The competition rules pulled on Sep 8 contain no explicit religious-content clause — this is a creative and filter-risk decision, not a compliance one. Generation platforms do commonly reject religious imagery, and the film is stronger for defining its own terms.

reduction.why: Time, and the fact that every line kept is one the film would be lesser without: the thesis, the brother, the button, and the want that ends it.

changes.what: The ending reversed. Alder is now the brother who learns the right lesson.
changes.why: Author's note. The conquest line stays with Alder and stays verbatim, but it is now his first instinct rather than his conclusion: it arrives as voice-over over the push-in, and then he sets it down and says the film's last new line on camera, smiling. Wren, who was the excited one, has turned away to stare at the keepers and does not look back — so the want does not leave the film, it changes brother. The dark cloud moves off Alder and sits behind Wren.
changes.departs_from_source: The novel gives the elder brother the conquest reading and says it guided him for the next ten years. The film keeps the sentence and reverses who it ends up describing.
